In mathematics, specifically in [[order theory]] and [[functional analysis]], if <math>C</math> is a cone at 0 in a vector space <math>X</math> such that <math>0 \in C,</math> then a subset <math>S \subseteq X</math> is said to be '''<math>C</math>-saturated''' if <math>S = [S]_C,</math> where <math>[S]_C := (S + C) \cap (S - C).</math> 
Given a subset <math>S \subseteq X,</math> the '''<math>C</math>-saturated hull''' of <math>S</math> is the smallest <math>C</math>-saturated subset of <math>X</math> that contains <math>S.</math>{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|pp=215–222}} 
If <math>\mathcal{F}</math> is a collection of subsets of <math>X</math> then <math>\left[ \mathcal{F} \right]_C := \left\{ [F]_C : F \in \mathcal{F} \right\}.</math>

If <math>\mathcal{T}</math> is a collection of subsets of <math>X</math> and if <math>\mathcal{F}</math> is a subset of <math>\mathcal{T}</math> then <math>\mathcal{F}</math> is a '''fundamental subfamily''' of <math>\mathcal{T}</math> if every <math>T \in \mathcal{T}</math> is contained as a subset of some element of <math>\mathcal{F}.</math> 
If <math>\mathcal{G}</math> is a family of subsets of a TVS <math>X</math> then a cone <math>C</math> in <math>X</math> is called a '''<math>\mathcal{G}</math>-cone''' if <math>\left\{ \overline{[G]_C} : G \in \mathcal{G} \right\}</math> is a fundamental subfamily of <math>\mathcal{G}</math> and <math>C</math> is a '''strict <math>\mathcal{G}</math>-cone''' if <math>\left\{ [B]_C : B \in \mathcal{B} \right\}</math> is a fundamental subfamily of <math>\mathcal{B}.</math>{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|pp=215–222}}

<math>C</math>-saturated sets play an important role in the theory of [[ordered topological vector space]]s and [[topological vector lattice]]s.

== Properties ==

If <math>X</math> is an ordered vector space with positive cone <math>C</math> then <math>[S]_C = \bigcup \left\{ [x, y] : x, y \in S \right\}.</math>{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|pp=215–222}}

The map <math>S \mapsto [S]_C</math> is increasing; that is, if <math>R \subseteq S</math> then <math>[R]_C \subseteq [S]_C.</math> 
If <math>S</math> is convex then so is <math>[S]_C.</math> When <math>X</math> is considered as a vector field over <math>\R,</math> then if <math>S</math> is [[Balanced set|balanced]] then so is <math>[S]_C.</math>{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|pp=215–222}}

If <math>\mathcal{F}</math> is a [[filter base]] (resp. a filter) in <math>X</math> then the same is true of <math>\left[ \mathcal{F} \right]_C := \left\{ [ F ]_C : F \in \mathcal{F} \right\}.</math>
